subject: DPA review: SCCs, role delegation gaps and Order Form notes
messages:
From: Sarah Gomes <sarah.gomes@cortexhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@cortexhealth.com
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 15:21:00 -0700
Subject: Initial DPA redlines + SCCs questions

Hi Karthik,

Attached are our team's initial redlines to the DPA and a short table of questions related to SCC application and role delegation (processor/controller). Main items:
- Cortex is asking for a clearer processor-only role for Redwood's hosted API paths; we need confirmation that telemetry/audit logs we request are scoped and do not make us a joint controller.
- We see a gap on subprocessor notification cadence (30 vs 14 days) — current Order Form references 30 days but your standard DPA mentions 14. Which applies?
- Data export commitments for EU-hosted records: Cortex wants an option to keep data within EU regions. Please point to the technical controls and whether Private deployment is required to guarantee locality.

Attachments: CortexHealth_DPA_Initial_Redlines.docx (docx), OrderForm_ExportControls_Table.xlsx (xlsx)

Can your team review and advise on which items require legal redlines vs product/ops commitments? We are hoping to close the commercial terms by 2027-09-10.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Gomes
Head of Legal Operations
Cortex Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Gomes <sarah.gomes@cortexhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + SCCs questions

Hi Sarah — thanks for the packet and the timeline. I looped in Ben (contracts) and Marissa (privacy ops) to split review. High level responses below; detailed redlines from legal will follow by EOD Monday.

Quick answers:
- Processor vs controller: Redwood's position is processor for customer data flows through the inference API. Telemetry we collect is operational (errors, latency) and retained for debugging; we agree to narrow access controls and put explicit language in the DPA about telemetry pseudonymization and retention window. Legal to propose language.
- Subprocessor notice: We're OK to align to 30 days in the Order Form for Cortex's contract if legal signs off; Ben will confirm.
- EU data locality: Hosted plan offers region pinning but does not guarantee physical-only processing unless Cortex subscribes to Dedicated or Private. Marissa: please add a short note about what we can offer and any extra cost.

Action items:
1) Ben: prepare redline focusing on SCCs references, subprocessor notice, and telemetry clause.
2) Marissa: prepare an ops note on region pinning and a proposed phrasing for the Order Form export table.
3) Karthik (me): coordinate legal/product alignment and set a quick sync with Cortex next week.

I can do a 30-min call Tue 2027-09-07 10:00am PT — does that work for you?

Regards,
Karthik
Head of Legal (Contracts) | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Gomes <sarah.gomes@cortexhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + SCCs questions

Karthik / Sarah — draft redline attached (excerpted below). I left alternative language in square brackets for Cortex to pick.

-- excerpt start --
Section 2.2 (Roles): Redwood shall act as a processor with respect to Personal Data processed on behalf of Cortex. Notwithstanding the foregoing, [for telemetry and operational metadata described in Annex A, Redwood shall process such data as a processor and shall pseudonymize or aggregate such data prior to any use for product analytics; retention of telemetry shall be limited to 90 days unless required for security incident investigation].

Section 5.3 (Subprocessors): Redwood will provide written notice of new subprocessors [no less than 30 days] prior to engagement and will honor customer-specific objection processes set out in the Order Form.

Annex B (Data Transfers / SCCs): Redwood confirms SCCs will be appended to the DPA; any additional transfer addendum (TIA) requests that impose localization constraints that cannot be met by Hosted must be scoped as an Order Form add-on (Dedicated/private).
-- excerpt end --

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Redline_20270906.docx (docx)

Ben notes:
- We should avoid making the DPA promise physical-only residency for hosted without a contractual add-on.
- For Cortex's telemetry concerns, Marissa and infra will share a short operations memo (what data, who can access, retention, and redaction policy).

If Sarah is OK, I'll push the redline into the shared Drive and drop a tracked version into HubSpot.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Gomes <sarah.gomes@cortexhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@cortexhealth.com
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + SCCs questions

Ben / Karthik — thanks for the quick turnaround and the alternative language — helpful. A few clarifying points before we book the call:
1) Telemetry: Cortex's security team needs explicit confirmation that telemetry cannot be repurposed to reconstruct patient-level records. The pseudonymization language is good but we need a definition and the 90-day cap looks reasonable.
2) Subprocessor notice: We accept 30 days if Redwood commits to maintain an up-to-date public subprocessor list and notify customers by email for material changes.
3) SCCs and TIA: Our procurement team will push for SCCs + a transfer impact addendum documenting the legal basis and risk assessment. If Hosted can't meet localization constraints, we'll either proceed with the TIA and an add-on or evaluate Dedicated. We will bring procurement to the call.

Can we keep the call to 30 minutes and focus on telemetry definition, subprocessor cadence, and Order Form export table? Tue 2027-09-07 10:00am PT works for our side.

Regards,
Sarah

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Gomes <sarah.gomes@cortexhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + SCCs questions — prep + ops note

Thanks team — quick prep note ahead of the 10:00am PT call:

Ops memo summary (attached to Drive):
- Telemetry set: request_id, request_timestamps, error_codes, model_name, token_count. We will not log raw prompt/response content for EU-pinned requests unless Cortex opts in for enhanced support and signs a support-data-access addendum.
- Access & retention: telemetry access limited to SRE and support engineers on a need-to-know basis; 90-day retention default; 365 days for security incident retention only with notice.
- Subprocessors: public list hosted at https://status.redwood.com/subprocessors (we can include this URL in the DPA). Notification emails are sent for material changes; non-material updates reflected in the public list.
- Export controls: OrderForm_ExportControls_Table.xlsx maps which features require Dedicated/Private for physical-only guarantees. Hosted = region pinning (logical), Dedicated = contractual locality.

Next steps: Ben will finalize tracked redline after call and we'll upload to the shared Drive (link in HubSpot). Karthik will follow up with Cortex procurement if the TIA is requested.

Attachments (referenced): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDPA-Review, OrderForm_ExportControls_Table.xlsx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Privacy Operations Lead | Redwood Inference
